summary: This is a Mol Labs hypothesis card (N16) proposing a research design to test whether oral creatine that raises plasma creatine without a concurrent prefrontal/gray-matter ³¹P-MRS PCr (or PCr/Pi) rise fails to rescue working memory and processing speed under sleep restriction. The document is a pre-experimental discussion/proposal (TRL 1–2), cataloguing existing literature as prior art and defining a prediction with specific thresholds, but no original experiments have been run. The core claim is a "compartment-discordance assumption-kill" — that plasma creatine elevation alone is insufficient as a pharmacodynamic surrogate for cognitive rescue under sleep deprivation.

content_blocks.title: Hypothesis Overview and Claim (N16)
content_blocks.content: Hypothesis N16 proposes that on a pre-registered sleep-restriction panel with oral creatine, paired plasma/serum creatine, concurrent prefrontal/GM ³¹P-MRS PCr (or PCr/Pi), and WM/processing-speed measures: under oral creatine that elevates plasma/serum creatine WITHOUT concurrent prefrontal/GM PCr (or PCr/Pi) rise, sleep-restriction WM/processing-speed rescue fails. Threshold: rescue Δ ≤20% of concurrent plasma-up/PCr-up stratum Δ on the same panel. This is framed as an 'assumption-kill / compartment-discordance' test. Execution status: NOT_RUN. No original experiments have been conducted.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch — Compartment-Discordance
content_blocks.content: Oral creatine can raise plasma/serum creatine and, separately, brain total creatine (¹H-MRS). Under sleep deprivation, cognition can co-move with ³¹P-MRS PCr/Pi / HEP. No published head-to-head study stratifies plasma-up by concurrent prefrontal/GM PCr co-movement and tests whether plasma-up/PCr-flat fails sleep-restriction WM/processing-speed rescue that plasma-up/PCr-up retains. Preferred design: same-panel oral creatine + plasma/serum Cr + concurrent ³¹P-MRS PCr (or PCr/Pi) + WM/processing-speed under sleep restriction (optional ¹H-MRS tCr). Competing caveats: plasma fails to rise / PCr unmeasurable / underpowered strata / assay-identity mismatch leave the test inconclusive rather than refuted.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art — Literature Evidence Base
content_blocks.content:
Four key prior art references are cited:
1. PMID 38418482 (Gordji-Nejad 2024, Sci Rep): ~21 h sleep deprivation + oral creatine; cognitive performance/processing speed improve vs placebo with concurrent ³¹P-MRS PCr/Pi, ATP, HEP changes + ¹H-MRS tCr/tNAA. Does NOT report plasma/serum creatine as cognitive PD; not a plasma-up/PCr-flat fail H2H.
2. PMID 40520504 (2025, Front Neurosci): Reanalysis of Gordji HEP dataset; sleep-deprivation hemispheric asymmetry in HEP consumption balanced by creatine (PCr/Pi and ATP shifts). Not a plasma-compartment discordance H2H.
3. PMID 10484486 (Dechent 1999, Am J Physiol): Oral creatine-monohydrate raises brain total creatine on quantitative ¹H-MRS in healthy volunteers (region-variable CNS uptake). No concurrent ³¹P PCr × plasma × SD WM panel.
4. PMID 16416332 (McMorris 2006, Psychopharmacology): Creatine + sleep deprivation with mild exercise; less cognitive/psychomotor/mood deterioration vs placebo; blood catecholamines/cortisol measured — NOT plasma creatine as cognitive PD; not plasma-up/PCr-flat fail H2H.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Measured vs. Unknown
content_blocks.content:
Baseline measured (from literature):
- SD+creatine cognition with concurrent ³¹P HEP co-movement: LITERATURE (PMID 38418482; 40520504)
- Brain tCr rise after oral creatine: LITERATURE (PMID 10484486)
- SD+creatine cognition with catecholamine/cortisol blood work: LITERATURE (PMID 16416332) — plasma Cr not assayed as cognitive PD

Baseline UNKNOWN:
- Matched plasma-up without concurrent prefrontal/GM PCr (or PCr/Pi) rise → WM/processing-speed rescue fails under sleep restriction: UNKNOWN (soft-complete plasma|serum creatine ∩ ³¹P|PCr ∩ WM|cognition ∩ sleep = 0; Gordji∩plasma = 0)
- Plasma-up/PCr-flat rescue Δ ≤20% of concurrent plasma-up/PCr-up stratum Δ: PREDICTION only

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations and Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content:
Actionable limitations:
1. N1–N15 do not prove N16 — N4 mapped Gordji SD+creatine cognition with ³¹P HEP co-movement and left subject-level PCr-vs-plasma superiority UNKNOWN; N15 is residual modafinil PVT under DAT-matched block; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated fail.
2. Parallel PCr/cognition ≠ plasma-discordance test — Gordji 2024/2025 move cognition and ³¹P HEP together; Dechent shows brain tCr rise; McMorris assays catecholamines/cortisol not plasma Cr as PD — none stratify plasma-up by concurrent PCr co-movement.
3. Plasma under-measured, not falsified; lock same-panel oral creatine + plasma/serum Cr + concurrent prefrontal/GM ³¹P-MRS PCr (or PCr/Pi) + WM/processing-speed under sleep restriction.

Refutation criteria: On the pre-registered sleep-restriction panel, under oral creatine with verified plasma/serum creatine elevation AND concurrent prefrontal/GM PCr (or PCr/Pi) flat, WM/processing-speed rescue still succeeds (rescue Δ >20% of concurrent plasma-up/PCr-up stratum Δ) — so plasma-up alone suffices and compartment-discordance fails — when plasma-rise, PCr-flatness, and power/assay artifacts are ruled out.

key_findings: Hypothesis N16 is a pre-experimental proposal (NOT_RUN) — no original experiments have been conducted; TRL is effectively TRL 1 (concept/hypothesis stage).

Core claim: oral creatine elevating plasma/serum creatine WITHOUT concurrent prefrontal/GM ³¹P-MRS PCr (or PCr/Pi) rise will fail to rescue WM/processing-speed under sleep restriction (rescue Δ ≤20% of plasma-up/PCr-up stratum Δ).

Gordji-Nejad 2024 (PMID 38418482) demonstrated cognitive/processing-speed improvement vs placebo under ~21 h sleep deprivation + oral creatine with concurrent ³¹P-MRS PCr/Pi, ATP, HEP changes — but did NOT report plasma/serum creatine as cognitive pharmacodynamic marker.
Gordji 2025 reanalysis (PMID 40520504) confirmed hemispheric asymmetry in HEP consumption balanced by creatine (PCr/Pi and ATP shifts) — not a plasma-compartment discordance H2H.

Dechent 1999 (PMID 10484486) showed oral creatine-monohydrate raises brain total creatine on quantitative ¹H-MRS in healthy volunteers (region-variable CNS uptake) — no concurrent ³¹P PCr × plasma × SD WM panel.

McMorris 2006 (PMID 16416332) showed less cognitive/psychomotor/mood deterioration vs placebo under creatine + SD with mild exercise; measured catecholamines/cortisol but NOT plasma creatine as cognitive PD.

Soft-complete search result: matched plasma-up/PCr-flat × WM-fail under SD H2H = 0 (UNKNOWN); no published study stratifies plasma-up by concurrent prefrontal/GM PCr co-movement and tests WM rescue failure.

Proposed assay design requires: same-panel oral creatine + paired plasma/serum Cr + concurrent prefrontal/GM ³¹P-MRS PCr (or PCr/Pi) + WM/processing-speed under sleep restriction + optional ¹H-MRS tCr + plasma-up/PCr-up positive-control stratum.
Competing inconclusive outcomes pre-specified: plasma fails to rise / PCr unmeasurable / underpowered strata / assay-identity mismatch.
Kill cost tier 1; estimated time to refute: 4 weeks; IP class: compartment-discordance; vault hold: no.
